title: Unit – 5 : Session – 8 : SLO – 2  |  Defining and Binding Event Handlers to Widgets
sections: 1. Binding a function to a button — either pass it at creation: tk.Button(root, text="Go", command=my_func); or use the generic binder: button.bind("<Button-1>", my_handler) where the handler receives an event object.

2. When a bound function is triggered — the event loop detects the event and calls the handler synchronously on the GUI thread; the handler runs to completion, then control returns to mainloop() and the UI updates.

3. Sharing handlers — yes. Multiple widgets can register the same handler; inside it, event.widget (or the command's shared state) identifies which widget fired, e.g. one on_key handler for several Entry fields.
